A good post-mortem is not a trial. Nobody is there to find a guilty person. The question is simple: what would we do differently next time? Start with the facts: what happened, and when. Then look back honestly. In hindsight, almost every problem looks avoidable, so be careful. Ask one question: could we have foreseen this with the information we had at the time? If the answer is yes, it was an oversight, and you need a new process. If the answer is no, it was bad luck, and you need a better contingency plan. Use simple, clear sentences. If we had checked the data earlier, we would have saved three weeks. That sentence is not about blame. It is about the next project. Finish with three lessons learned, and give each one an owner.

Hi Carlos, it is Tom. I just saw the March payroll report, and I wanted to thank you. Every salary was correct. Do you remember those three extra weeks of testing? If we had not done them, about four hundred people would have received the wrong salary on their first payday with Northway. That would have been a disaster for morale. And honestly, if you had not helped me with the committee slides, I think I would have downplayed the problem. So, thank you. For the post-mortem, I have one suggestion. Next time, let us check the old data before we sign the plan, not after. Talk soon.
